To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the average human summary contains 55% of all words that occur in a source document, and that the average human summaries of the same source document agree on 22% of all words.

(a) the vocabulary agreement between model summaries and the source document is about 55%; (b) the vocabulary agreement among model summaries of the same source document is about half this amount, or about 25%; and (c) the vocabulary agreement for all model summaries of all source documents, which is a measure of the vocabulary agreement among all model summaries, is about 22%.
(1) the vocabulary of a summary is a subset of the vocabulary of the source document and (2) different summaries of the source document agree on only 55% of their vocabulary.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following issues: (1) What is the relationship between the vocabulary of a summary and that of the source document from which it is derived?
how to improve the quality of the summary, in terms of both the quantity and the relevance of the information it contains, as well as the quality of its presentation.
the development and evaluation of a new approach to summarization that is based on a model of the information in a document and the way it is conveyed.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the vocabulary of manually-written summaries of news documents is not a superset of the vocabulary of the source documents.
there is a great need for a more detailed and comprehensive analysis of the vocabulary of manually-written model summaries.
the vocabulary agreement between the summaries and the source documents is not very strong.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have shown that the vocabulary of a manually-produced summary is not a superset of the vocabulary of the source document, and that the vocabulary of one summary is not a subset of the vocabulary of another summary of the same document.

the vocabulary agreement is a result of the fact that the source documents are written in a style which makes them amenable to summarization by a human reader, but which makes the same summarization difficult or impossible for a computer.

vocabulary overlap between model summaries and source documents can be expected to be less than 55%, and that vocabulary overlap between pairs of summaries of the same text can be expected to fall below 22%.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the performance of such systems is likely to be limited to 20% agreement with human summaries.

a system that extracts vocabulary from the source document and uses it to compose a summary will be able to reproduce at most 22% of the vocabulary of the source document in its summary, and at most 55% of its vocabulary if it also extracts vocabulary from a set of manually-written summaries.
the vocabulary of a summary can be very different from the source document, and that the vocabulary of one summary can be very dissimilar to the vocabulary of another summary of the same document.
